extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, HR/personnel officials, federal employees, unions, and legal practitioners involved in adverse action and classification issues
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing when federal employees retain accrued competitive-service status and adverse-action/procedural rights upon movements of positions or employees into or within the excepted service, and the related coverage/exclusion rules and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of accrued rights upon involuntary move
rubrics_metrics.description: A competitive service employee whose position is first listed under Schedule A, B, C, or any future excepted service schedule remains in the competitive service for the purposes of status and protections, while the employee continues to occupy the position or any other positions to which the employee is moved involuntarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounded in longstanding precedent (e.g., Roth and Loudermill). OPM updates 5 CFR 212.401(b) to state this explicitly, covering moves to any future excepted schedules. The rule clarifies this retention applies while the employee occupies the position or any subsequent positions to which the employee is involuntarily moved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary move relinquishes rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee relinquishes accrued rights by voluntarily seeking, accepting, and encumbering a position that explicitly results in a loss of, or different, rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a voluntary movement from the competitive service to Schedule C requires an acknowledgment from the employee that adverse action rights would be waived. Distinguishing voluntary from involuntary moves is the key factor in retention analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'employee' for adverse-action coverage (5 U.S.C. 7501/7511)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of subchapter II and appeal rights, ‘employees’ include individuals who have completed probationary/trial periods or meet current continuous service durational requirements (e.g., 1- or 2-year thresholds) in the same or similar positions under other than temporary appointments limited to 1 or 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM revised regulatory language to conform to Federal Circuit decisions (Van Wersch, McCormick) interpreting statutory accrual conditions. The statutory 'same or similar positions' language primarily governs accrual, and some individuals otherwise considered probationers may actually meet appeal-rights requirements if they satisfy the other statutory conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage for suspensions of 14 days or less (5 CFR 752.201(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if an agency intends to suspend for 14 days or less an employee in the competitive service who is serving a probationary or trial period, the employee is entitled to the procedural rights provided under 5 U.S.C. 7503 if the individual has completed 1 year of current continuous service in the same or similar position under other than a temporary appointment limited to 1 year or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment conforms subpart B to Federal Circuit precedent (Van Wersch, McCormick). OPM revised section 752.201(b)(1) accordingly and aligns regulatory coverage with statutory language and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of current continuous employment
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Current continuous employment’ is defined as a period of employment or service immediately preceding an adverse action without a break in Federal civilian employment of a workday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined in 5 CFR 752.201(d) and 752.402. Remote work or telework does not break continuous service; the definition does not turn on physical presence in an office. Traditional performance management tools address work monitoring where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions for confidential/policy-influencing positions (5 CFR 752.201(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees in positions determined to be of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character as defined in 5 CFR 210.102 are excluded from coverage under subpart B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM will revise §752.201(c)(7) to clarify that this exclusion does not apply to incumbents who were moved involuntarily into such positions after they had already accrued rights under §752.201(b). The exclusion is intended to implement statutory limits but must be read consistent with precedent protecting accruals on involuntary moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of part 752 subpart D (removals, suspensions >14 days, reductions, furloughs)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who has accrued adverse action rights by completing probation or a current continuous service requirement and who occupies a position moved from the competitive service into the excepted service, or from one excepted schedule to another, is covered by the regulatory requirements for removal, suspension for more than 14 days, reduction in grade or pay, or furlough for 30 days or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to §752.401(c) and related provisions reinforce that accrued statutory procedural rights cannot be taken away by involuntary moves. These changes align regulations with how courts and the MSPB have interpreted similar rights when employees change jobs or agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision to 5 CFR 212.401(b) referencing competitive status definition
rubrics_metrics.description: §212.401(b) is revised to establish that a competitive service employee whose position is first listed involuntarily under any future excepted service schedule remains in the competitive service, and the regulation will reference the definition of competitive status in §212.301.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reference to §212.301 reduces risk of inconsistent interpretation and ensures uniform language regarding who has competitive status. The revision also anticipates future excepted schedules and clarifies coverage during involuntary sequences of moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of involuntary moves immaterial to retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Once status and rights are accrued, the number of times an employee is moved involuntarily does not affect retention of those rights so long as the sequence is not broken by a voluntary acceptance of a different position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM will revise regulatory text to make explicit that retention is not limited by the number of involuntary moves; agencies cannot strip accrued rights by repeatedly moving employees involuntarily to dissimilar positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions under 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories are excluded from accrual/retention under §7511(b), including political appointments requiring Senate confirmation, Schedule C political appointees, and presidential appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM emphasizes it is not extending civil service protections to employees whom statute expressly excludes. The regulatory clarifications define and apply these exceptions consistent with statutory text and legislative history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retained adverse-action procedural protections upon conversion when incumbent had status
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee who was serving in a position in the competitive service when OPM authorized its conversion to Schedule C and is still serving in that position continues to have adverse action protections (e.g., 30-day notice specifying reasons, right to reply personally and in writing, right to representation, consideration of reply, written decision stating reasons, appeal to MSPB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects historical CSC guidance and longstanding practice (cited advisory and Roth). The listed procedural rights are the standard protections afforded under 5 U.S.C. 7513 and part 752 when status is retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming regulations to Federal Circuit precedent (Van Wersch, McCormick)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory language (e.g., 5 CFR 752.201(b)(1)) is revised to align with Federal Circuit precedents interpreting 5 U.S.C. 7511(a)(1) and 5 U.S.C. 7501, including understanding statutory alternatives and durational requirements that determine who is an ‘employee’ for appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM's changes reflect the courts' interpretations that some individuals traditionally viewed as probationers may nonetheless be ‘employees’ for purposes of appeal rights if they meet other statutory conditions; regulatory text is harmonized accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify coverage language to include employees moved involuntarily to any subsequent position
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions in 752.201(b)(1),(b)(2),(b)(6) and corresponding sections are revised to apply where the employee is moved involuntarily and continues to occupy that position or any other position to which the employee is moved involuntarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision prevents agencies from defeating accrued rights by moving an employee to a dissimilar position and ensures coverage follows the involuntary sequence rather than being limited to the initial position alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention limited to employees who have 'accrued' rights by meeting statutory conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights are retained only for individuals who have accrued status and procedural rights by meeting the statutory accrual conditions (e.g., completion of probationary/trial periods or current continuous service thresholds under 5 U.S.C. 7501/7511).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule distinguishes accrual (how rights are earned) from retention (whether those earned rights continue after a move). Accrual requirements remain the gateway to retention protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM rulemaking authority and interpretive basis
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM's amendments elaborate upon and clarify retention of rights upon involuntary moves and further define exceptions in 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2) based on OPM's interpretation supported by statutory text, legislative and statutory history, and precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM notes it is clarifying longstanding regulatory and judicial constructions (citing Roth, Loudermill, other decisions) and is not creating unauthorized new rights for employees excluded by statute. Precedent and history are used as interpretive tools where congressional intent is not explicit in text.
